title: Tidewater 2.4 Release Notes
key_sentences: Tidewater 2.4 adds resumable transfers, a faster change scanner and a new configuration format.
This document explains how to install the release and what changed since version 2.3.
The configuration file lives in the project root and is read every time the tool starts.
Use the preview flag to see what a sync would do without copying anything.
Report problems on the project tracker and include the output of the status command.

rows: Number of tries before a transfer fails
Copy new and changed files to the target
List files that differ from the target

list_items.text: 1. Download the archive for your platform and unpack it into any folder.
2. Add the folder to your PATH.
3. Check the installation by running the command below.
Resumable transfers: an interrupted copy continues where it stopped.
A change scanner that is about three times faster on large folders.
A new configuration format based on YAML.
Clearer error messages that name the file and the reason.
– The old .ini configuration file is no longer read.
– Exit code 4 now means a partial transfer and not an error.
1. Paths longer than 260 characters are skipped on older Windows versions.
2. The status command may report a file twice if it is renamed during a scan.

code:
sync:
  source: ./project
  target: //nas01/backup/project
  exclude:
    - "*.tmp"
    - ".cache/"
retry:
  attempts: 5
  delay_seconds: 30

tidewater sync --preview
3 files would be copied, 1 file would be removed
notes: The coloured band holds the title and a one-line subtitle (the subtitle is body text, not furniture and not a key sentence). Three heading levels are used: the title (1), sections (2) and sub-sections (3). Three code blocks in all: two on page 1 (a shell command, then a YAML file) and one on page 2 (a preview run), in that order. Inline code spans inside sentences are ordinary text. Install steps are TYPED '1.' '2.' '3.' with a hanging indent; the list under 'What is new' is drawn by CSS (no marker typed); breaking changes use typed en dashes. The options table has a monospaced first column. The footer lines (left text, right page number) are furniture.
